## Solution

**Interpretation.** For real $x$, write $(-1)^x = e^{i\pi x}$ (principal branch). The integrand becomes

$$
e^{i\pi x}\,e^{-\frac{\pi x}{2}(nx+1)}
= e^{\,i\pi x-\frac{\pi n}{2}x^{2}-\frac{\pi}{2}x}
= e^{-\frac{\pi n}{2}x^{2}+\pi\left(i-\tfrac12\right)x}.
$$

**Gaussian evaluation.** Completing the square,

$$
-\frac{\pi n}{2}x^{2}+\pi\!\left(i-\tfrac12\right)x
= -\frac{\pi n}{2}\!\left(x-\frac{i-\tfrac12}{n}\right)^{\!2}
+ \frac{\pi\left(i-\tfrac12\right)^{2}}{2n}.
$$

Since $\operatorname{Re}(\pi n/2)>0$ (as $n>0$), the shift of the Gaussian contour is legitimate, giving

$$
I=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-\frac{\pi n}{2}(x-a)^{2}}dx\cdot
\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi(i-\tfrac12)^{2}}{2n}\right)
=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n}}\;\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi(i-\tfrac12)^{2}}{2n}\right).
$$

Now $(i-\tfrac12)^{2}=i^{2}-i+\tfrac14=-\tfrac34-i$, so

$$
\frac{\pi(i-\tfrac12)^{2}}{2n}
= -\frac{3\pi}{8n}-\frac{i\pi}{2n},
$$

and therefore

$$
I=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n}}\;e^{-3\pi/(8n)}\;e^{-i\pi/(2n)}.
$$

**Determining $n$.** The modulus of the integral is

$$
|I|=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n}}\;e^{-3\pi/(8n)}.
$$

Requiring $|I|=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ (the integral's magnitude matching the prescribed real value $\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$) gives

$$
\sqrt{2}\,e^{-3\pi/(8n)}=1
\;\Longrightarrow\;
e^{3\pi/(8n)}=\sqrt{2}
\;\Longrightarrow\;
\frac{3\pi}{8n}=\frac{\ln 2}{2}.
$$

Solving,

$$
\boxed{\,n=\frac{3\pi}{4\ln 2}\,}.
$$

**Verification.** At $n=\dfrac{3\pi}{4\ln 2}$,

$$
\frac{3\pi}{8n}=\frac{3\pi}{8}\cdot\frac{4\ln 2}{3\pi}=\frac{\ln 2}{2},
\qquad
e^{-3\pi/(8n)}=e^{-\ln 2/2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},
$$

so $|I|=\sqrt{2/n}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, as required.

## Solution

**Interpretation.** For real $x$, write $(-1)^x = e^{i\pi x}$ (principal branch). The integrand becomes

$$
e^{i\pi x}\,e^{-\frac{\pi x}{2}(nx+1)}
= e^{\,i\pi x-\frac{\pi n}{2}x^{2}-\frac{\pi}{2}x}
= e^{-\frac{\pi n}{2}x^{2}+\pi\left(i-\tfrac12\right)x}.
$$

**Gaussian evaluation.** Completing the square,

$$
-\frac{\pi n}{2}x^{2}+\pi\!\left(i-\tfrac12\right)x
= -\frac{\pi n}{2}\!\left(x-\frac{i-\tfrac12}{n}\right)^{\!2}
+ \frac{\pi\left(i-\tfrac12\right)^{2}}{2n}.
$$

Since $\operatorname{Re}(\pi n/2)>0$ (as $n>0$), the shift of the Gaussian contour is legitimate, giving

$$
I=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-\frac{\pi n}{2}(x-a)^{2}}dx\cdot
\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi(i-\tfrac12)^{2}}{2n}\right)
=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n}}\;\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi(i-\tfrac12)^{2}}{2n}\right).
$$

Now $(i-\tfrac12)^{2}=i^{2}-i+\tfrac14=-\tfrac34-i$, so

$$
\frac{\pi(i-\tfrac12)^{2}}{2n}
= -\frac{3\pi}{8n}-\frac{i\pi}{2n},
$$

and therefore

$$
I=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n}}\;e^{-3\pi/(8n)}\;e^{-i\pi/(2n)}.
$$

**Determining $n$.** The modulus of the integral is

$$
|I|=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n}}\;e^{-3\pi/(8n)}.
$$

Requiring $|I|=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ (the integral's magnitude matching the prescribed real value $\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$) gives

$$
\sqrt{2}\,e^{-3\pi/(8n)}=1
\;\Longrightarrow\;
e^{3\pi/(8n)}=\sqrt{2}
\;\Longrightarrow\;
\frac{3\pi}{8n}=\frac{\ln 2}{2}.
$$

Solving,

$$
\boxed{\,n=\frac{3\pi}{4\ln 2}\,}.
$$

**Verification.** At $n=\dfrac{3\pi}{4\ln 2}$,

$$
\frac{3\pi}{8n}=\frac{3\pi}{8}\cdot\frac{4\ln 2}{3\pi}=\frac{\ln 2}{2},
\qquad
e^{-3\pi/(8n)}=e^{-\ln 2/2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},
$$

so $|I|=\sqrt{2/n}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, as required.
